title: Tempest watch brief - 2026-09-07
content:
Shift: Tempest watch (EU evening -> APAC overlap)
Shift owners: Maya Desai (lead), Omar Ruiz (backup)
Timezone: primary notes in UTC; local roundup at 2026-09-07T20:00Z

Quick summary for incoming shift:
- Quiet baseline until 19:12Z, then two correlated alerts: embedding-service 95th latency jump and cache hit-rate drop for prefix-KV. Impacted customer traffic: routed to fallback model variant for ~18 minutes.
- One pager escalation (SRE-4821) opened for ongoing investigation of cache eviction pattern.
- Mitigation completed: scaled embedding-service pool + temporary config rollback of aggressive compaction (config: kv/compaction.enabled=true -> false). Result: latency recovered to baseline by 19:30Z.
- Secondary issue: intermittent 500s from router-proxy to hosted-api when model fallback triggered. Follow-up ticket SRE-4833 assigned to Priya.

Detailed timeline (UTC):
- 19:11:14 - Alerts: metric alert embedding-service.p95 > 750ms (5m window) and prefix-kv.hit_rate < 60%
- 19:12:03 - Pager: oncall (Maya) paged, initial check of dashboards (embed-rt, kv-hitrate, node-GC)
- 19:13:20 - Observed pattern: increased GC frequency on a subset of kv nodes (hostnames kv-eu-*) and concurrent disk iowait spikes on those hosts.
- 19:16:05 - Scaled embedding-service from 6 -> 10 replicas (autoscale policy manual burst) to absorb load; also temporarily disabled kv compaction (rolled back config change that was deployed 2026-09-06 03:40Z).
- 19:21:40 - Router-proxy started returning 502/500 for ~1% of requests; root cause appears to be short-lived TCP connection churn when fallback model spin-up occurred.
- 19:24:50 - Rolled restart of kv-eu-03 to clear GC pressure; monitored iowait and heap stats.
- 19:30:22 - p95 returned to normal (under 300ms), cache hit-rate climbing back to 87% by 19:35. Noise legacy alerts closed; incident marked as mitigated.

Immediate action items completed during shift:
- Manual burst scale + rollback compaction flag (Maya)
- Restarted kv-eu-03; observed heap churn reduction (Omar)
- Notified Support & CS for affected customer routes (Liam) with ETA for RCA

Observations and hypotheses:
- The compaction job that was autoscheduled on 2026-09-06 likely interacted poorly with small-EBS-backed kv instances during peak; compaction caused high iowait and frequent GC cycles. We suspect that disk throughput throttling triggered longer GC pause times.
- Router-proxy 500s correlate with model fallback churn; proxy health checks sometimes treat transient model cold-starts as backend failures. Might need to tweak health-check grace period for model variants.

Runbook draft snippets to add/update (for review):
- Title: kv-host-gc-spike-response (draft)
  - Preconditions: have kubectl access to infra-prod cluster, SRE role, runbook-owner listed
  - Quick checks: curl /metrics embedding-service, grafana:embed-rt, grafana:kv-node-health, ssh to kv node and check dmesg/iostat/top -H, check disk saturation (iostat -x 1 3)
  - Take actions: if iowait > 20% and compaction job running -> cancel compaction (kubectl patch configmap kv-config --patch '{"data":{"compaction.enabled":"false"}}'), scale replicas, schedule rolling restart of pods with node-affinity to avoid hitting same EBS devices
  - Post-incident: tag nodes, escalate to infra if EBS pressure recurring, open ticket SRE-<num> for capacity plan
- Title: router-proxy-fallback-grace (draft)
  - Symptoms: 5xx spike coincident with model variant failover
  - Fix candidates: increase backend grace window on healthcheck from 2s -> 6s for model-variants; add short queuing buffer during cold-starts; add metric router.proxy.backend_failure_rate and alert threshold at 0.5% sustained

Unresolved items / follow-ups (owners assigned):
- SRE-4821 (Maya): RCA doc - confirm compaction schedule, enumerate nodes affected, collect iostat traces, attach heapdump if available. ETA: 2026-09-10.
- SRE-4833 (Priya): Router-proxy healthcheck tweak PR + load test to validate no regression. ETA: 2026-09-09. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/762
- Capacity review (Omar): evaluate EBS burst credits across kv fleet and consider moving hot kv shards to NVMe-backed hosts. Deliverable: short recommendation note by 2026-09-14.
- Support follow-up (Liam): customer postmortem summary and templated message for affected customers. ETA: 2026-09-08 12:00Z

Notes to incoming shift (practical checklist):
- Check dashboards: Embed p95, Prefix-KV hit rate, KV node iowait, Router-proxy 5xx rate (links in incident panel)
- Confirm that compaction.enabled=false is still set in prod-config for kv; if changed, escalate immediately (audit: configmaps history)
- Monitor SRE-4821 sensor: any new compaction runs scheduled by cronjob on kv-compactor namespace? kill if needed and notify infra
- If p95 climbs > 500ms for >10m, do manual burst scale and open immediate page; do not rely on autoscaler alone because autoscale observed sluggishness in hotspots

Other contextual items and micro-logs (copied from incident chat):
- 19:17 Maya: "looks like compaction kicked on - iowait skyrocketed on kv-eu-03"
- 19:18 Priya: "spinning up more embed replicas now, but router is seeing some failed connects"
- 19:23 Liam: "support notified, customer route ABC-42 hit fallback - filing CS note"

Retention / housekeeping:
- This doc is a working handoff; please add comments inline for runbook steps that are unclear.
- When RCA is final, we will prune this doc and move a sanitized summary to Confluence (page id: 89123) and close SRE-4821/4833 accordingly.

Post-shift checklist for oncall rotation lead (incoming):
- Acknowledge SRE-4821 and SRE-4833 ownership in Jira; update watchers and priority.
- Confirm compaction flag and schedule change on prod-config or cronjobs.
- Run quick smoke test on router-proxy healthcheck config in staging and report results.

Random notes / items for future runbook edits (brainstorm):
- Add a short script: diagnose-kv-gc.sh that aggregates top, jstack, iostat, and uploads to S3; make it part of runbook.
- Consider metric: kv.compaction.running_count and kv.node.iowait_95 to alert earlier.

Acknowledgements: thanks to Priya for quick scaling and Omar for node restart coordination.

End of shift: Maya signing off 2026-09-07T21:05Z

Incoming next: Priya Kapoor (APAC overlap) - please reach out in #sre on Slack if you see anything odd or need handover clarifications.
